description: Default calibration prompt set for head-budget softmax-mass measurement (~8 short prompts; each ~400-700 tokens after tokenization on Qwen3/Bonsai). Replace via `rmlx kv-calibrate --recipe head_budget --prompts <path>` for arch-specific tuning.
prompts: Describe in detail how a relational database executes a multi-table join. Walk through the cost-based optimizer, index selection, hash join versus merge join, the physical plan tree, and the runtime accounting of memory budgets. Be specific about PostgreSQL's behavior and explain how the planner handles a missing statistic, then how parallel query workers split the build phase across multiple CPUs while preserving deterministic output ordering downstream of the join.

Walk through the steady-state token-generation loop of a transformer language model in production. Start from the tokenizer pre-tokenization step, then describe the embedding lookup, the per-layer attention computation, the KV-cache update, the feedforward block, residual connections, the final norm, the unembedding projection, the logit-softmax, and the sampler. For each step, name the dominant cost (memory bandwidth, compute throughput, kernel launch overhead) and explain how attention bandwidth scales with context length.

Compare three strategies for serving an LLM with diverse concurrent requests: vLLM-style continuous batching with paged attention, static batching with padded sequences, and per-request streaming with no batching. For each, describe expected behavior on a mixed workload that includes 100-token-prompt completions, 16K-token retrieval-augmented prompts, and a long-running conversation that has accumulated 32K tokens of history. Explain which strategy delivers the lowest median latency, the lowest tail latency, and the highest throughput.

Explain how Apple Silicon's unified memory architecture changes the data-movement model for ML inference relative to a discrete-GPU CUDA system. Cover: the absence of explicit device transfers, how Metal's command queues interact with the CPU side, how the wired memory limit affects long-context models, the cost of unified memory pressure when other processes are running, and the operational implications for a multi-tenant inference server.

Describe the lifecycle of a TCP connection from the kernel's perspective, beginning with the three-way handshake and ending with the four-way close. Cover the socket state machine, the role of the TIME_WAIT state in protecting against duplicate segments, congestion control on the sender (slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit), and what happens to in-flight data when one side calls close while the receive buffer still contains unread bytes. Explain how Linux's TCP_QUICKACK affects interactive workloads.

Outline a working specification for a content-addressed object store similar to S3 or IPFS. Describe the immutable object identifier scheme, the hash-tree manifest format for multi-part objects, the consistency model across replicas, the garbage-collection process for unreferenced blocks, the access-control surface, and the strategy for handling small-object overhead. Address how the system handles a write that races with a delete, and how clients verify integrity end-to-end without trusting the gateway.

Walk through the formal definition of a Bayesian belief update, then apply it to a concrete diagnostic example: a medical test with 90 percent sensitivity and 95 percent specificity used in a population with 1 percent prevalence. Compute the posterior probability of disease given a positive result, then a negative result. Discuss how the posterior changes when the test is run twice, and why naive multiplication of likelihood ratios can be misleading when results are not conditionally independent.

Survey the design tradeoffs of a modern garbage collector for a managed runtime. Compare generational copying, mark-sweep, mark-compact, concurrent mark-and-sweep, and region-based G1-style collectors. For each, describe the pause-time characteristics, throughput cost, fragmentation behavior, write-barrier overhead, and suitability for workloads with very large heaps. Conclude with a recommendation for a server running a 200 GB heap on a many-core machine that requires sub-10ms tail latencies.
